entities.summary:
Constantine Lascaris was a Greek scholar and grammarian, one of the key figures in the revival of Greek learning in Italy during the Renaissance, born in Constantinople around 1400.


 Lascaris' most notable contribution was the compilation of the Palatine Corpus, a comprehensive collection of Greek texts that helped establish a standardized system for Greek grammar and lexicography.


 His work had a profound impact on the intellectual landscape of 15th-century Italy, influencing prominent scholars such as Petrarch and Boccaccio.


 Despite his significant contributions to the field of classical studies, Lascaris' own life remains somewhat of a mystery, with few biographical details available to historians.
